findings.evidence: `grep -rn "universalNormEDS_apply" TauCeti` → no hits; `Universal.lean:128-131` declares `@[simp] theorem universalNormEDS_def : universalNormEDS = normEDS (X B) (X C) (X D) := (rfl)`, whose own docstring (`:126`) states `@[simp]` rewrites the head constant so applied occurrences normalise either way; `Invariant/NormEDS.lean:131-134` uses the named rewrite with the comment "the rewrite under `invarNum` needs the named equation".
findings.fix: Restrict it: `mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero (by simpa only [universalNormEDS_def] using universalNormEDS_ne_zero hk)` (add `ne_eq` to the list if the match needs it), and update the comment at lines 138-140 to name the equation lemma instead of describing it as "the `@[simp]` equation lemma".
findings.issue: `by simpa using universalNormEDS_ne_zero hk` leaves the whole default simp set to bridge `universalNormEDS k ≠ 0` to `normEDS (X B) (X C) (X D) k ≠ 0`; the single lemma actually doing the work is unnamed, so any future simp lemma about `normEDS` over `MvPolynomial NormEDSParam ℤ` can derail it opaquely. The PR description defends the naked `simpa` as insulation against #3361 renaming `universalNormEDS_apply` to `universalNormEDS_def`, but in this checkout only `universalNormEDS_def` exists and `Invariant/NormEDS.lean:134` already rewrites with that name by hand.

summary: Proofs are otherwise robust and well-commented, but the one step that discharges the nonzerodivisor hypothesis runs the full default simp set to fire a single named equation lemma, and the stated reason for not naming it is contradicted by the head tree.
